items.title: Sudan: Drought and war push Darfur and Kordofan towards famine
items.summary: The risk of famine is growing in parts of Sudan already torn apart by war, as a severe El Niño drought makes life even harder in Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, the UN-backed global hunger monitor warned on Monday.

items.title: Myanmar Military Steps Up Airstrikes in Rakhine as Ground Offensive Stalls
items.summary: Crisis Group expert Thomas Kean examines why the Myanmar military’s faltering counteroffensive and escalating air attacks have further dimmed prospects for a ceasefire in Rakhine State.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s fragile transition – economic strain, Israeli incursions and progress towards elections
items.summary: The Security Council is meeting on Syria as the country’s transition faces pressure on several fronts. Economic hardship is fuelling unrest, Israeli incursions continue in the south and sectarian tensions persist in Sweida, even as Damascus reports progress on its chemical weapons programme and talks about future elections. Millions, meanwhile, remain displaced. Follow live below and go here for full meetings coverage.

items.title: ‘Efficiency has limits’: UNHCR chief warns refugee protection is buckling under cuts
items.summary: The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year – and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.

items.title: Toward a Thaw in the Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict
items.summary: Hostilities between Cambodia and Thailand ceased in late 2025, after two rounds of combat along the frontier. But the truce is under growing strain. To avoid more war, the two countries should restore normal diplomatic ties and resume work on demarcating their shared border.

items.title: Sustaining livelihoods amid crisis in Gaza
items.summary: Nidaa, Hanaa and Hanin have different stories, but share a common thread: the determination to build something of their own and keep it going despite extraordinary challenges facing them in war-ravaged Gaza.

items.title: Sixth Committee Evaluates Ongoing Efforts to Conclude Treaty on Crimes against Humanity
items.summary: As work continues towards a legally binding treaty on preventing and punishing crimes against humanity, speakers in the Sixth Committee (Legal) today underlined the need for a future convention that enjoys broad support and closes a long-persisting gap in the international criminal architecture.

items.title: Africa Must Have Stronger Ownership of Its Vast Resources, Fairer International Partnerships, Greater Investment, Speakers Tell General Assembly
items.summary: Speakers in the General Assembly called for stronger African ownership of Africa’s vast resources, fairer international partnerships and greater investment, warning that illicit financial flows, mounting debt and declining development assistance continue to undermine the continent’s progress.

items.title: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears
items.summary: Nearly 10 years after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement to end a decades-long insurgency, the deal is under strain from growing insecurity – and the UN’s top official in the country says it cannot be allowed to falter.

items.title: ‘Stark Gaps Remain’ in Achieving Development Goals, Second Committee Hears as 2030 Deadline Nears
items.summary: With just over three years remaining to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, a senior United Nations official warned the Second Committee (Economic and Financial) today that “stark gaps remain” in efforts to meet development targets, particularly those affecting the world’s poorest people.

items.title: Humans Must Remain in Control, First Committee Hears, as Security Trust Frays
items.summary: At a time when many States warn that the global disarmament architecture is failing, an area of convergence emerged during the First Committee’s (Disarmament and International Security) general debate today: countries across geopolitical divides increasingly agree that humans, not algorithms, must retain ultimate control over the use of force.
